cr1_comp_15.FINAL_COMPARATIVE_VERDICT: Across the 18 evaluated solutions, direct optimization under corrected COST-E3D restructures rather than uniformly replaces the historical reevaluated set: both sets are internally nondominated (9/9), 78/81 cross-set pairs are incomparable, dominance is sparse and bidirectional (C-to-H 1; H-to-C 2), and joint Rank 1 retains 8 H and 7 C solutions. C has greater anchored hypervolume at r5, r10 and r20 and a substantially lower median f1 with modestly higher median f2/f3, while H retains all observed marginal objective extremes and has greater reciprocal coverage. This establishes finite-set trade-off restructuring under a common nominal TMAX horizon, not convergence, global optimality, between-seed robustness or statistical superiority of the algorithm.

Results_implications.implication: All 9 historical R1 solutions reevaluated under corrected COST-E3D and all 9 CORRECTED_R1 solutions were internally nondominated within their respective finite sets.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Within-set status only; neither set is a true/global Pareto front.

Results_implications.implication: Exact cross-set dominance was sparse and bidirectional: C dominated H in 1 pair, whereas H dominated C in 2 pairs.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Exact pairwise relations among the 18 evaluated solutions.

Results_implications.implication: Exact set coverage was 1/9 (11.11111111111111%) for C over H and 2/9 (22.22222222222222%) for H over C.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Coverage is asymmetric and finite-set specific.

Results_implications.implication: The joint nondominated set of the 18 evaluated solutions contained 8 H and 7 C solutions (15/18 total).
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Joint Rank 1 is not a true/global Pareto front.

Results_implications.implication: C introduced no new observed marginal objective extremes; H retained all observed global marginal extremes.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Observed marginal extremes of these finite sets.

Results_implications.implication: C occupied narrower observed marginal intervals than H in f1, f2, and f3.
At the primary r10 reference, anchored hypervolume was 0.9749820881940048 for H and 1.0099628901072748 for C; C>H also held at the prespecified r5 and r20 references.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Anchored, commonly normalized hypervolume under the three frozen reference points only.

Results_implications.implication: Relative to H, C had a 33.807045718015644% lower median f1, a 3.1995544935821214% higher median f2, and a 3.8585642103238946% higher median f3.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: All objectives are minimized; these are descriptive medians of finite sets.

Results_implications.implication: All 18 cases were compared under the common nominal maximum-horizon regime COMMON_TMAX_19P9H.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Fixed maximum horizon, not free normal termination or identical temporal trajectories.

Results_implications.implication: No exact cross-dominance relation was classified as numerically fragile under the frozen diagnostic.
Results_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Diagnostic sensitivity only; exact dominance remained unchanged.

Discussion_implications.implication: Direct optimization under corrected COST-E3D did not uniformly replace the historical reevaluated trade-off set.
The combined evidence is consistent with trade-off restructuring rather than a uniform directional shift.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Descriptive synthesis, not a formal classification or causal proof.

Discussion_implications.implication: C was concentrated within a narrower observed objective-space region without new marginal extremes, while 7 of its 9 solutions remained in joint Rank 1.
The greater anchored hypervolume of C indicates greater coverage of the objective space defined by the frozen common anchors and reference points.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: It does not measure distance to a true front or demonstrate convergence.

Discussion_implications.implication: C's markedly lower median f1 was accompanied by moderately higher median f2 and f3, indicating an observed trade-off rather than global superiority.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Finite-set central tendencies; no statistical inference.

Discussion_implications.implication: H retains scientific and design value because 8/9 H solutions remain in joint Rank 1, H locally dominates two C solutions, preserves the observed marginal extremes, and has greater reciprocal coverage.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Historical R1 solutions were reevaluated, not reoptimized, under corrected COST-E3D.

Discussion_implications.implication: C contributes new compromise information because 7/9 C solutions remain in joint Rank 1, C04 dominates H05, and HV_C exceeds HV_H at r5/r10/r20.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: No single best solution or global superiority follows.

Discussion_implications.implication: The C-region concentration hypothesis is only partially supported and is interpreted as involving multiple trade-off mechanisms rather than one unique physical mechanism.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Mechanistic attribution remains limited by persisted evidence.

Discussion_implications.implication: The economic interpretation concerns specific modeled operating energy cost and must remain distinct from total modeled operating energy cost or comprehensive economic cost.
Discussion_implications.mandatory_qualifier: Excludes CAPEX, maintenance, labor, TCO, and commercial total cost.

Discussion_implications.implication: The environmental interpretation concerns specific modeled operational CO2 as implemented, not life-cycle environmental impact.
The common TMAX regime removes a trivial nominal-horizon difference as an H-versus-C explanation, but it does not imply identical temporal trajectories.

Limitations.implication: Only one CORRECTED_R1 run is available (seed 61001); between-seed variability is not established.
CORRECTED_R1 stopped after reaching MaxGenerations=50; this is not evidence of convergence.
The compared sets are finite and no independent true/global Pareto front is available.
The nine H and nine C points are not independent optimizer replicates and cannot support statistical performance inference.
All 18 cases share COMMON_TMAX_19P9H, so results concern a fixed maximum horizon rather than free normal termination.
Irradiacion is not available in the persisted validated evidence, preventing direct quantitative attribution to Irradiacion.

f2 is modeled operating energy cost; it excludes CAPEX, maintenance, labor, TCO, and commercial total cost.
f3 is modeled operational CO2 as implemented, not a life-cycle carbon footprint or total environmental impact.
The CO2/CO2e label requires editorial reconciliation before final manuscript insertion.
H consists of historical solutions generated under an earlier formulation and later reevaluated, not directly reoptimized, under corrected COST-E3D.
Limitations.mandatory_qualifier: Do not call H a corrected Pareto front.
